sections.theory:
Exercise

Q 1. Choose the correct one from the given options.

1. Which one of the following is quantitative chemical analysis?

a. Salt analysis   b. Titration   c. Flame test   d. Bromine-water test

2. C₂H₆O is the molecular formula of (i) ethanol (ii) methanol (iii) dimethyl ether (iv) diethyl ether

a. (i) and (ii)   b. (ii) and (iii)   c. (i) and (iii)   d. (ii) and (v)

3. Which one of the following techniques is mainly used for determination of functional group in a compound?

a. IR Spectroscopy   b. NMR   c. UV/ Visible spectroscopy   d. Mass spectroscopy

4. Two different compounds will always give different absorption peak in ______ region of IR.

a. 1500–625 cm⁻¹   b. 4000–1500 cm⁻¹   c. 3000–2500 cm⁻¹   d. 3500–1500 cm⁻¹

5. Which one of the following methods, relatively gives more information about the structure of an organic compound?

a. Mass Spectroscopy   b. NMR Spectroscopy   c. IR Spectroscopy   d. UV-Visible Spectroscopy

6. A mass spectrum is shown below.

Which one of the following compound gives complete mass spectrum illustrated?

a. CO₂   b. N₂   c. C₃H₈   d. Mixture of CH₄ and N₂

7. The wavelength range of UV region is from

a. 400–800 nm.   b. 800–1200 nm.   c. 1200–1600 nm.   d. 10–400 nm.

8. Which one of the following hydrocarbon produces a proton NMR spectrum with more than one peak?

a. Methane   b. Ethane   c. Butane   d. Cyclobutane

9. How many signals/peaks would you expect in the proton NMR spectrum of 1,1-dicholorethane?

a. 2   b. 4   c. 6   d. 8

10. How many types of protons are there in butanoic acid?

a. 8   b. 2   c. 6   d. 4

11. In combustion analysis water is absorbed by

a. Mg(ClO₄)₂   b. NaOH   c. CuO   d. CuSO₄

12. Modern methods of analysis are superior to classical one because

a. they give more accurate results.   b. small amounts of chemicals are used.   c. less time consuming.   d. all of the above.

13. Which one is an in-plane bending vibration?

a. Wagging   b. Scissoring   c. Twisting   d. None of these

14. Pi to pi star transition occurs in

a. ethane.   b. ethene.   c. ethyl alcohol.   d. methyl chloride.

15. Which one is NMR inactive nucleus?

a. ³¹C   b. ¹H   c. ¹⁵N   d. ¹⁶O

Q2. Write short answers of the following questions.

i. What is meant by stretching and bending vibrations?

ii. If a compound shows 100% transmittance, what do we infer from it?

iii. What does λmax mean to you?

iv. Define and explain Bear-Lambert’s Law.

v. Why tetramethyl silane is used as a standard in NMR spectroscopy?

vi. Explain the use of ionization chamber in mass spectrometer.

vii. Why magnesium perchlorate is used as H₂O absorber?

viii. Why modern method of analysis is superior over classical method of analysis?

sections.content:
Exercise

Q 1. Choose the correct one from the given options.

1. Which one of the following is quantitative chemical analysis?

a. Salt analysis b. Titration c. Flame test d. Bromine-water test

2. C₂H₆O is the molecular formula of (i) ethanol (ii) methanol (iii) dimethyl ether (iv) diethyl ether

a. (i) and (ii) b. (ii) and (iii) c. (i) and (iii) d. (ii) and (v)

3. Which one of the following techniques is mainly used for determination of functional group in a compound?

a. IR Spectroscopy b. NMR c. UV/ Visible spectroscopy d. Mass spectroscopy

4. Two different compounds will always give different absorption peak in ______ region of IR.

a. 1500–625 cm⁻¹ b. 4000–1500 cm⁻¹ c. 3000–2500 cm⁻¹ d. 3500–1500 cm⁻¹

5. Which one of the following methods, relatively gives more information about the structure of an organic compound?

a. Mass Spectroscopy b. NMR Spectroscopy c. IR Spectroscopy d. UV-Visible Spectroscopy

6. A mass spectrum is shown below.

Which one of the following compound gives complete mass spectrum illustrated?

a. CO₂ b. N₂ c. C₃H₈ d. Mixture of CH₄ and N₂

7. The wavelength range of UV region is from

a. 400–800 nm. b. 800–1200 nm. c. 1200–1600 nm. d. 10–400 nm.

8. Which one of the following hydrocarbon produces a proton NMR spectrum with more than one peak?

a. Methane b. Ethane c. Butane d. Cyclobutane

9. How many signals/peaks would you expect in the proton NMR spectrum of 1,1-dicholorethane?

a. 2 b. 4 c. 6 d. 8

10. How many types of protons are there in butanoic acid?

a. 8 b. 2 c. 6 d. 4

11. In combustion analysis water is absorbed by

a. Mg(ClO₄)₂ b. NaOH c. CuO d. CuSO₄

12. Modern methods of analysis are superior to classical one because

a. they give more accurate results. b. small amounts of chemicals are used. c. less time consuming. d. all of the above.

13. Which one is an in-plane bending vibration?

a. Wagging b. Scissoring c. Twisting d. None of these

14. Pi to pi star transition occurs in

a. ethane. b. ethene. c. ethyl alcohol. d. methyl chloride.

15. Which one is NMR inactive nucleus?

a. ³¹C b. ¹H c. ¹⁵N d. ¹⁶O

Q2. Write short answers of the following questions.

i. What is meant by stretching and bending vibrations?

ii. If a compound shows 100% transmittance, what do we infer from it?

iii. What does λmax mean to you?

iv. Define and explain Bear-Lambert’s Law.

v. Why tetramethyl silane is used as a standard in NMR spectroscopy?

vi. Explain the use of ionization chamber in mass spectrometer.

vii. Why magnesium perchlorate is used as H₂O absorber?

viii. Why modern method of analysis is superior over classical method of analysis?
